summary: Nintendo's real-time village life series, covering the main console/handheld games, design and party spinoffs, mobile Pocket Camp, and the Switch 2 edition of New Horizons.

entries.title: Animal Crossing

emulation.notes: Dolphin can improve GameCube image quality; language accessibility depends on version.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: GameCube emulation at high internal resolution

primary.why: For the original Animal Crossing family, Doubutsu no Mori e+ is the most content-complete GameCube revision, adding new and refined content over the earlier Nintendo 64/GameCube versions; the international GameCube Animal Crossing remains the English fallback.
primary.how_to_play: Play Doubutsu no Mori e+ on GameCube or Dolphin if Japanese is acceptable; use the international GameCube Animal Crossing for English accessibility.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official English release of the most complete e+ revision exists.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: Wild World

emulation.notes: DS emulation can improve display scaling while preserving the dual-screen layout.

primary.why: Wild World is a DS-exclusive mainline entry with no later port or enhanced edition.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS/3DS hardware or DS emulation with a legally dumped cartridge.

entries.remaster_caveats: Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection-era online features are no longer available through the original service.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: City Folk

emulation.notes: Dolphin can raise internal resolution for the highest-fidelity preservation route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Wii emulation at high internal resolution

primary.why: City Folk, also released as Let's Go to the City in PAL regions, is a Wii-exclusive mainline entry with no later port or enhanced edition.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Wii/Wii U backward compatibility or Dolphin with a legally dumped disc for higher internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original Wii online services are no longer the normal official route.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: New Leaf
entries.definitive_edition: Animal Crossing: New Leaf - Welcome amiibo

emulation.notes: 3DS emulation can increase resolution, but official route is 3DS hardware with the update.

primary.why: The free Welcome amiibo update turns New Leaf into the expanded version, adding amiibo support and additional features while keeping the base game.
primary.how_to_play: Play Animal Crossing: New Leaf on Nintendo 3DS with the Welcome amiibo update installed, or use the Welcome amiibo cartridge release.

entries.remaster_caveats: 3DS online-service changes affect online features, but the local single-player content remains the core route.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: Happy Home Designer

primary.why: Happy Home Designer is a 3DS-exclusive design spinoff and has no later enhanced release.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 3DS hardware or 3DS emulation with a legally dumped cartridge.

entries.remaster_caveats: Happy Home Paradise is a later New Horizons DLC successor, not an enhanced release of this game.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: Amiibo Festival

emulation.notes: Official route is Wii U hardware; Cemu is a preservation fallback if amiibo data is legally available.

primary.why: Amiibo Festival is a Wii U-exclusive party spinoff built around Animal Crossing amiibo figures/cards, with no later port or enhanced edition.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Wii U hardware with required compatible Animal Crossing amiibo.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires compatible amiibo for the intended experience.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp

primary.why: The original free-to-play Pocket Camp ended service on November 28, 2024, and Nintendo replaced it with Pocket Camp Complete, a paid app containing previously released content without additional in-game purchases.
primary.how_to_play: Buy and install Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp Complete on a compatible iOS or Android device.

entries.remaster_caveats: Some original online/social live-service behavior does not carry forward exactly into Complete.

entries.title: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
entries.definitive_edition: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition plus Happy Home Paradise and update 3.0

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch 2 hardware for the official best route.

primary.version: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition plus Happy Home Paradise and free 3.0 update
primary.why: The Switch 2 Edition is the highest-fidelity official route and adds enhanced Switch 2 features, while the free 3.0 update and Happy Home Paradise DLC make the content package more complete.
primary.how_to_play: Play Animal Crossing: New Horizons - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition on Switch 2 with the latest update and Happy Home Paradise installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: Happy Home Paradise is paid DLC; some 3.0 features and online functions may require Nintendo Switch Online.

entries.title: Animal Crossing
entries.definitive_edition: Animal Crossing / Dobutsu no Mori+ enhanced GameCube release

emulation.notes: Original GameCube hardware is the cleanest route for accessory behavior; Dolphin is a preservation fallback but GBA/e-Reader features need extra setup.

primary.version: Animal Crossing / Dobutsu no Mori+ enhanced GameCube release
primary.why: The GameCube release is the enhanced and localized console version, with GBA-link, e-Reader, multiplayer-town, and playable NES-game features documented for this generation of the game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GameCube release on original hardware with a memory card; add a Game Boy Advance, link cable, and e-Reader/cards only if you want the accessory-locked extras.

entries.remaster_caveats: No current official re-release exists; some GameCube extras require legacy accessories or event/card data.
